title: Man killed in a police shootout was responsible for double murder, not the accused on trial: defence lawyer
subtitle: Defence tells jurors accused Kamal Hassan was at the murder scene in a downtown Toronto short-term rental condo but it was a now dead man, Kwasi Skene-Peters, who shot and killed Mohamed Dirie and Abdiweli Abdullahi shortly before 7 a.m. on June 28, 2015.
article: A man killed in a police shootout was the person who executed two men inside a downtown Toronto condo - not Kamal Hassan, who is on trial for the double murder, his lawyer told a jury Tuesday.

Hassan will testify he was present in the short-term rental unit at 36 Lisgar St., near King St.W. and Dufferin St., when Kwasi Skene-Peters fatally shot Mohamed Dirie and Abdiweli Abdullahi, both 26, just before 7 a.m. on June 28, 2015, Adele Monaco said.

"You will hear that it was Kwasi Skene-Peters and not Mr. Hassan who shot and killed both Mr. Dirie and Mr. Abdullahi," the defence lawyer said during her opening remarks. "You will hear that Kwasi Skene-Peters used the gun that he had on him, and then he took Mr. Dirie's gun to shoot Mr. Abdullahi who was asleep in the bedroom."
Hassan will testify how Skene-Peters then removed Dirie's prominent gold necklace and his watch and then shot him one final time in the face, she said.

The jury has seen elevator surveillance video, recorded at 10 Eddystone Ave. an hour after the shootings, showing Skene-Peters wearing a large gold necklace - which he didn't have on earlier - and Hassan appearing to re-enact the murders.
Prosecutor David Mitchell told the jury the "video is silent but it speaks for itself."
Monaco also showed the jury a cellphone video, obtained by the defence earlier this month from Hassan's friend. It shows Skene-Peters and Dirie waving guns around.
"We're not saying the video speaks for itself. We're saying seeing is believing," Monaco said.

A forensic expert will testify the two-tone-coloured firearm Dirie appears to be holding cannot be excluded as being the same firearm recovered from Skene-Peters' shootout with the police, she said. Nor can it be excluded as one of the firearms used in the condo.
The expert will also testify Skene-Peters is holding what appears to be a nine-millimetre firearm that could have generated the jacket casings and bullet fragments at the Lisgar condo, Monaco said.

After the killings, Toronto police issued arrest warrants for Hassan and Skene-Peters. Police located Skene-Peters outside a downtown nightclub on July 25, 2015. A gun battle ensued and Skene-Peters died after officers shot him in the chest.

Forensic analysis determined a black 9-mm semi-automatic handgun he dropped was not the 9-mm firearm used in the 36 Lisgar St. murders. But another handgun recovered nearby was found to be the same .40 calibre handgun used in the double murders.
Before prosecutors closed their case Friday, the jurors heard about the criminal records of three dead men: the two victims and Skene-Peters.

Abdullahi had convictions for crack cocaine, assault with a weapon, possessing a loaded handgun, and breaching bail conditions. Dirie had convictions for robbery with an imitation firearm, disarming a police officer and conspiracy to traffic pot.
Skene-Peters was, the jury has heard, no law-abiding citizen. He had numerous convictions including several firearms offences.
The jury returns to the Superior Court of Justice courthouse Thursday to hear the continuation of the defence case.
